newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end flat, South-North tension lingers.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end flat, South-North tension lingers.

text.p: Stocks closed nearly flat on Saturday after fluctuating narrowly as growing tension on the Korean Peninsula after Pyongyang's submarine infiltration into the South dampened sentiment, brokers said.
"The South-North military tension continues to discourage buying sentiment, especially by foreign investors," said Yoo Jae-kyong, a broker with Daishin Securities.
Brokers said overall sentiment would remain weak next week.
The composite index ended 0.88 point higher at 777.31.
Yoo said the index would move between 760 and 800 next week with buying focused mostly on selected shares.
Volume totalled 22.83 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 38.66 million on Friday.
Gainers outpaced losers 506 to 320 with 154 unchanged.
Samil Pharmaceutical rose 400 won to 34,200 on good earnings prospects.
Daeyoung Electronics, a specialised maker of military-use radios, went limit-up, gaining 2,000 won to 35,600 on expectations of rising orders.
